Calibration records: logging a calibration, and what the logs hold

pdmS7 documentation

Source: vignettes/calibration-log.Rmd
calibration-log.Rmd

Manual calibration is judgement: a hydrologist reads a hydrograph, changes a parameter, and decides whether the model is better. A calibration can be defended later only if that judgement was recorded as it happened and cannot be quietly rewritten. The calibration log does this. Every action writes one entry to a project folder: who, when, which data and parameters, the scores, and the reasoning. Entries are never edited, each carries a checksum of the one before, and a report is generated from them.

This article walks through one calibration, from project start to sign-off, then opens the logs up: what files they are, what is in them, and how they guard against being quietly changed. The design record explains the decisions behind it. The same steps are available without code in the app, calibration_app().

Who is writing

Every entry records a declared name and role, with the operating-system login. Roles follow the governance framework: a Custodian does the calibration; a Steward (or Delegated Steward) signs it off; the Owner is named as accountable.

options(pdmS7.user = "Ann Hydrologist", pdmS7.role = "custodian")

Set these once per session, or in .Renviron as PDMS7_USER and PDMS7_ROLE.

Starting the project 

project <- file.path(tempdir(), "brook-calibration")
start_calibration_project(
  project, catchment = "Example Brook", gauge = "99001", purpose = "Flood forecasting",
  area_km2 = 40, owner = "Deputy Director", steward = "Sam Steward"
)

The data here are synthetic: four months of hourly rainfall, and the flow of a “true” catchment with gauging noise and a three-day gap.

set.seed(42)
n <- 24 * 120
time <- seq(as.POSIXct("2023-10-01", tz = "UTC"), by = 3600, length.out = n)
forcing <- data.frame(
  time = time, rain = ifelse(stats::runif(n) < 0.07, stats::rgamma(n, 0.7, scale = 3), 0),
  pet = 0.06
)
truth <- pdm_presets("standard")
truth$area_km2 <- 40
truth$fc <- 1.15
truth$recharge$kg <- 1500
truth$surface$k1 <- 3
truth$surface$k2 <- 8
# The river is already flowing when the record starts: steady state, not empty stores.
truth_model <- pdm_from_config(truth)
observed <- run_pdm(truth_model, forcing,
                    initial_state_from_flow(truth_model, 0.3, 0.7))$output$q_m3s *
  exp(stats::rnorm(n, 0, 0.04))
observed[1500:1572] <- NA

Registering the data

Registration copies the data into the project, takes their checksums, records their quality, and fixes the scorecard: the calibration and validation windows, the headline score, the starting soil moisture and any warning thresholds. Every later run is scored the same way, so trials can be compared fairly. Rows before the calibration window are warm-up.

Thresholds may be flows or river levels. Levels are converted to flows through a rating table registered with the data, and a level outside the rating is refused rather than extrapolated.

rating <- data.frame(stage_m = c(0.2, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2), q_m3s = c(0.3, 0.8, 2.2, 5, 9))
thresholds <- data.frame(name = c("Flood Alert", "Flood Warning"), value = c(1.8, 1),
                         unit = c("flow", "level"))
reg <- register_data(
  project, forcing, observed,
  calibration = c("2023-10-15", "2023-12-31"),
  validation = c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-28"),
  headline = "nse", thresholds = thresholds, rating = rating,
  reasoning = "Gauge record checked against the station log.",
  wettest_years = 0
)
str(reg$summary[c("rows", "start", "end", "observed_missing", "observed_longest_gap")])
#> List of 5
#>  $ rows                : int 2880
#>  $ start               : chr "2023-10-01T00:00:00Z"
#>  $ end                 : chr "2024-01-28T23:00:00Z"
#>  $ observed_missing    : int 73
#>  $ observed_longest_gap: int 73

Choosing the structure 

start <- pdm_presets("standard")
start$area_km2 <- 40
select_structure(project, start,
                 reasoning = "Standard PDM as the starting point for a responsive clay catchment.")

The structure is run and scored like any trial, so it is the root of the calibration path.

Trials

preview_trial() runs a change without logging it, so you can look before you commit.

preview <- preview_trial(project, parent = 3, changes = c(fc = 1.15))
rows <- preview$rows[1:(24 * 30)]
parent_model <- pdm_from_config(start)
parent <- run_pdm(parent_model, forcing,
                  initial_state_from_flow(parent_model, observed[1], 0.7))$output$q_m3s
top <- max(observed[rows], parent[rows], preview$simulated[rows], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.25
par(mar = c(3, 4.2, 0.6, 0.6))
plot(time[rows], observed[rows], pch = 16, cex = 0.3, col = pal[5], xlab = "",
     ylab = "Flow (m3/s)", ylim = c(0, top))
lines(time[rows], parent[rows], col = pal[7], lwd = 1.5)
lines(time[rows], preview$simulated[rows], col = pal[1], lwd = 1.5)
legend("topleft", c("observed", "parent (0003)", "preview"), bty = "n", horiz = TRUE,
       col = c(pal[5], pal[7], pal[1]), pch = c(16, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, 1, 1))

The preview against its parent over part of the calibration window. 

before <- unlist(project_trials(project)[1, c("nse", "volume_error", "kge_alpha")])
after <- unlist(preview$scores[c("nse", "volume_error", "kge_alpha")])
round(rbind(parent = before, preview = after), 3)
#>            nse volume_error kge_alpha
#> parent  -0.331       -0.285     1.459
#> preview -0.649       -0.141     1.915
dry <- function(v) sprintf("%.0f per cent too %s", abs(100 * v), if (v < 0) "dry" else "wet")

The volume error has gone from 29 per cent too dry to 14 per cent too dry, but the NSE has fallen: the variability ratio, 1.92, shows the peaks are now too large. The trial is still an improvement, because the water balance is closer and the peaks are a separate question. That judgement is the hydrologist’s, not the headline score’s, and the log records it with its reason:

log_trial(project, parent = 3, changes = c(fc = 1.15), verdict = "better",
          reasoning = paste0("Volume ", dry(before[["volume_error"]]),
                             "; raised the rainfall factor. Peaks now too big."))
log_trial(project, parent = 4, changes = c(recharge.kg = 500), verdict = "worse",
          reasoning = "Much faster recharge, to feed baseflow; far too much water now.")
log_trial(project, parent = 4, changes = c(recharge.kg = 1500), verdict = "better",
          reasoning = "A smaller change instead; volume and recessions both match.")
log_trial(project, parent = 6, changes = c(surface.k1 = 3, surface.k2 = 8),
          verdict = "better", reasoning = "Peaks slightly early; slowed the surface cascade.")

Trial 0005 was a dead end; trial 0006 went back to 0004 and tried a smaller change. The log keeps both, because a defensible calibration includes what was tried and rejected.

A short automatic calibration can polish the result. It is logged like a trial, with its bounds, seed and the table of every start.

auto <- log_auto_calibration(
  project, parent = 7, lower = c(surface.k1 = 1, surface.k2 = 3),
  upper = c(surface.k1 = 6, surface.k2 = 15), starts = 3, seed = 1,
  control = list(maxit = 30), reasoning = "Fine-tune the routing within physical bounds."
)
log_note(project, "The January gap is a logger fault, not low flow.", refers_to = 2)

Trials on the largest events

The headline score weighs every time step alike, so a change that sharpens the floods may barely move it. event_workbench() gathers a run’s largest events, ten unless you choose another number, screened for rises lost in the baseflow and gaps. workbench_try() reruns them with a change, in a fraction of a second, and plot_workbench() draws them before (blue) and after (vermillion), with each event’s peak and timing errors in its title:

wb <- event_workbench(project, entry = auto$id, n = 4)
wb
#> Events workbench: 4 largest events in the calibration window, from entry 0008
#> Median peak error -4%, timing +0.5 h, event NSE 0.97
delayed <- workbench_try(wb, c(td = 1))
plot_workbench(wb, delayed)

The four largest calibration events of the automatic calibration, and the same with a one-hour time delay.

In the app, the Events tab does the same on sliders: the surface stores, the time delay and the store shape b. Choose how many events to show, move a slider, and the events redraw. Save as trial logs the setting through log_trial() with your verdict and reasoning, so it joins the log like any other trial, and Check recessions draws the recession plot of the record and the model (recession_analysis()), to see that the low flows still fall at the right rate.

The calibration path 

trials <- project_trials(project)
trials[, .(id, type, parent, changes, verdict, nse = round(nse, 3),
           volume_error = round(volume_error, 3))]
#>        id               type parent                              changes
#>    <char>             <char> <char>                               <char>
#> 1:   0003 structure_selected   <NA>                                     
#> 2:   0004              trial   0003                         fc 1 -> 1.15
#> 3:   0005              trial   0004              recharge.kg 4000 -> 500
#> 4:   0006              trial   0004             recharge.kg 4000 -> 1500
#> 5:   0007              trial   0006 surface.k1 2 -> 3; surface.k2 4 -> 8
#> 6:   0008   auto_calibration   0007                                     
#>    verdict    nse volume_error
#>     <char>  <num>        <num>
#> 1:    <NA> -0.331       -0.285
#> 2:  better -0.649       -0.141
#> 3:   worse -0.217        0.359
#> 4:  better  0.677        0.001
#> 5:  better  0.985       -0.001
#> 6:    <NA>  0.985       -0.001
x <- seq_len(nrow(trials))
colour <- ifelse(trials$type == "auto_calibration", pal[1],
                 ifelse(is.na(trials$verdict), pal[5],
                        ifelse(trials$verdict == "better", pal[3], pal[6])))
plot(x, trials$nse, pch = 16, col = colour, cex = 1.6, xaxt = "n", xlab = "",
     ylab = "NSE, calibration window")
axis(1, at = x, labels = trials$id)
parents <- match(trials$parent, trials$id)
segments(x[parents], trials$nse[parents], x, trials$nse, col = pal[7])

Every run by its NSE on the calibration window. Lines join each run to its parent; colour shows the verdict.

Candidate and validation

The candidate is rerun before it is accepted, and must reproduce its recorded output exactly. Validation scores the validation window, once.

propose_candidate(project, entry = auto$id,
                  reasoning = "Best NSE with physically sensible time constants.")
val <- validate_candidate(project, reasoning = "Holds up on January.")
round(data.frame(calibration = unlist(val$calibration_scores),
                 validation = unlist(val$validation_scores))[c("nse", "kge", "volume_error",
                                                               "fdc_high"), ], 3)
#>              calibration validation
#> nse                0.985      0.972
#> kge                0.988      0.970
#> volume_error      -0.001     -0.001
#> fdc_high          -0.009     -0.019

Warning thresholds

Every run was also scored at both thresholds. An event is an episode above the threshold; a simulated crossing within six hours of an observed one is a hit, and exceedances less than a day apart count as one event.

pick <- function(scores, window) {
  metrics <- c("observed_events", "hits", "misses", "false_alarms", "pod", "far", "csi",
               "crossing_error_h", "csi_step")
  do.call(rbind, lapply(thresholds$name, function(t) {
    data.frame(threshold = t, window = window,
               lapply(stats::setNames(metrics, metrics), function(m) {
                 round(scores[[paste0(m, ":", t)]], 2)
               }), check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}
rbind(pick(val$calibration_scores, "calibration"), pick(val$validation_scores, "validation"))
#>       threshold      window observed_events hits misses false_alarms  pod far
#> 1   Flood Alert calibration              12    8      4            0 0.67   0
#> 2 Flood Warning calibration               4    4      0            0 1.00   0
#> 3   Flood Alert  validation               4    4      0            0 1.00   0
#> 4 Flood Warning  validation               3    2      1            0 0.67   0
#>    csi crossing_error_h csi_step
#> 1 0.67            -0.12     0.82
#> 2 1.00             0.00     0.78
#> 3 1.00             0.00     0.92
#> 4 0.67             0.50     0.69

Two lessons. First, a high NSE does not guarantee warning skill: in the calibration window the candidate scores an NSE of 0.99, yet misses 4 of the 12 Flood Alert events, because peaks near a threshold cross it or not on small errors. Second, event and step scores answer different questions. Step scores weight each event by its length, so a long flood simulated well dominates them and a short flood missed barely registers. Event scores count each flood once, which is how a warning service is judged, and they count a crossing an hour late as a hit, where steps count a miss and a false alarm. Here csi_step is the kinder score in 2 rows and the harsher in 2, so neither is simply more lenient. Note how few events there are: with 3 to 12 per window, one event moves POD by a twelfth or more, so read these scores alongside the counts. The report draws all thresholds and both windows on one performance diagram.

A project for a warning service can rank runs by a threshold score, with headline = "csi:Flood Warning" at registration. Automatic calibration can reward threshold skill too. Event counts change in steps, which a gradient optimiser cannot follow, so this uses the derivative-free Nelder-Mead method, with a continuous score to break ties:

log_auto_calibration(
  project, parent = 7, lower = c(surface.k1 = 1), upper = c(surface.k1 = 6),
  objective = "nse", method = "nelder_mead", threshold_objective = "Flood Warning",
  threshold_weight = 1, reasoning = "Tune routing for warning timing."
)

The entry records the method, the weighted objective and the number of model runs, so a reviewer can see what the optimiser was rewarded for.

Sign-off

Only a Steward or Delegated Steward can sign off, and not one who wrote any of the calibration. The package checks both the declared name and the login, so a Steward cannot sign off from the Custodian’s session:

options(pdmS7.user = "Sam Steward", pdmS7.role = "steward")
reviewed <- c(integrity = TRUE, data = TRUE, calibration_path = TRUE, validation = TRUE)
tryCatch(sign_off_project(project, "Accepted.", reviewed),
         error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
#> [1] "You wrote calibration entries in this project; another Steward must sign off"

In practice the Steward signs off on their own machine, or in the app. Below we stand in for that machine by giving the Steward a different login.

sign_off_project(project, "Reviewed the path, data and validation. Accepted for forecasting.",
                 reviewed)
read_project(project)$status
#> [1] "signed_off"

A signed-off project accepts nothing further until a Steward reopens it with a reason.

Integrity

verify_project() recomputes every checksum and, with rerun = TRUE, repeats every run.

checks <- verify_project(project, rerun = TRUE)
checks[, .N, by = .(check, ok)]
#>            check     ok     N
#>           <char> <lgcl> <int>
#> 1:     numbering   TRUE    12
#> 2:         chain   TRUE    12
#> 3:  data forcing   TRUE     1
#> 4: data observed   TRUE     1
#> 5:   data rating   TRUE     1
#> 6:        series   TRUE     2
#> 7:         rerun   TRUE     7

Now suppose someone tidies the reasoning of trial 0005 after the event:

file <- file.path(project, "entries", "0005-trial.yml")
original <- readLines(file)
writeLines(sub("far too much water", "a little too much water", original), file)
verify_project(project)[ok == FALSE]
#>     check  entry     ok                                      detail
#>    <char> <char> <lgcl>                                      <char>
#> 1:  chain   0006  FALSE Previous entry altered, removed or inserted
writeLines(original, file)

The edit is caught at the next entry, whose stored checksum no longer matches (the checksum chain shows how). Changed data files and runs that no longer reproduce are caught the same way.

The report 

build_report(project)

build_report() writes report/report.html, a single file with embedded figures that can be attached to a review, and a Markdown copy. It opens with the integrity result, then shows the data, the structure, the calibration path, the candidate’s hydrographs and flow-duration curves for both windows, parameter sensitivity, the sign-off and the final configuration with every entry’s checksum.

Tracing operational runs

Once a calibration is in use, the question changes from “how was it calibrated” to “which calibration produced this forecast”. The run log answers it. It is off by default.

register <- file.path(dirname(project), "approved.yml")
writeLines(c("projects:", paste0("  - ", basename(project))), register)
options(pdmS7.run_log = file.path(tempdir(), "runs.csv"), pdmS7.register = register,
        pdmS7.run_tag = "forecast 2024-02-01 06:00")
approved <- pdm_from_config(auto$configuration)
recent <- forcing[2700:2880, ]
forecast <- run_pdm(approved, recent)
check <- run_pdm(pdm_from_config(start), recent)
read_run_log()[, .(tag, fingerprint = substr(fingerprint, 1, 8), rows, status, approval,
                   project, sign_off)]
#>                          tag fingerprint  rows status   approval
#>                       <char>      <char> <int> <char>     <char>
#> 1: forecast 2024-02-01 06:00    12b38ad6   181     ok   approved
#> 2: forecast 2024-02-01 06:00    5d6cb444   181     ok unapproved
#>              project sign_off
#>               <char>   <char>
#> 1: brook-calibration     0012
#> 2:

The first run used the signed-off parameters and is marked approved, with the project and sign-off entry; the second used the uncalibrated structure and is marked unapproved. Neither was blocked. If the project is reopened, runs with the old parameters are marked superseded.

Summary

Step Function
Declare who you are options(pdmS7.user = , pdmS7.role = )
Start start_calibration_project()
Data, scorecard and thresholds register_data()
Structure select_structure()
Try, then log preview_trial(), log_trial(), log_auto_calibration(), log_note()
Decide propose_candidate(), validate_candidate()
Approve sign_off_project(), reopen_project()
Check and report verify_project(), build_report(), project_trials()
Trace use options(pdmS7.run_log = , pdmS7.register = ), read_run_log()

Inside the logs

pdmS7 keeps two kinds of log. A calibration log records how one model was calibrated: every decision, by whom, with which data and parameters, and why. A run log records every time a model is run, so any result can be traced to the parameters behind it. This part uses a small project of its own.

A small project to look inside 

set.seed(1)
n <- 24 * 40
time <- seq(as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC"), by = 3600, length.out = n)
forcing <- data.frame(time = time, pet = 0.05,
                      rain = ifelse(stats::runif(n) < 0.07, stats::rgamma(n, 0.7, scale = 3), 0))
truth <- pdm_presets("standard")
truth$area_km2 <- 30
truth_model <- pdm_from_config(truth)
observed <- run_pdm(truth_model, forcing,
                    initial_state_from_flow(truth_model, 0.6, 0.7))$output$q_m3s
options(pdmS7.user = "Ann Hydrologist", pdmS7.role = "custodian")
project <- file.path(tempdir(), "inside")
start_calibration_project(project, catchment = "Example Brook", gauge = "99003",
                          purpose = "Illustration", area_km2 = 30,
                          owner = "Deputy Director", steward = "Sam Steward")
register_data(project, forcing, observed, calibration = c(121, 600),
              validation = c(601, 800), test = c(801, n), wettest_years = 0)
start <- truth
start$fc <- 0.9
select_structure(project, start, "Standard PDM.")
log_trial(project, parent = 3, changes = c(fc = 1), verdict = "better",
          reasoning = "Volume was 10 per cent low.")
log_note(project, "Gauge checked against the station log.", refers_to = 2)
propose_candidate(project, entry = 4, reasoning = "Best so far.")
validate_candidate(project, "Holds on validation.")
test_candidate(project, "Holds on the final window.")

The project folder 

files <- list.files(project, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE)
files[!grepl("^report/", files)]
#>  [1] "data/0002/forcing.csv"               "data/0002/observed.csv"             
#>  [3] "entries/0001-project_start.yml"      "entries/0002-data_registered.yml"   
#>  [5] "entries/0003-structure_selected.yml" "entries/0004-trial.yml"             
#>  [7] "entries/0005-note.yml"               "entries/0006-candidate.yml"         
#>  [9] "entries/0007-validation.yml"         "entries/0008-test.yml"              
#> [11] "pdms7-project.yml"                   "series/0006.csv"                    
#> [13] "series/0007.csv"                     "series/0008.csv"
Path Holds
pdms7-project.yml Marks the folder as a project: format version and identifier
entries/ One YAML file per entry, numbered in the order written, never edited
data/0002/ Copies of the data registered by entry 0002, as CSV
series/ Full simulated and observed flow for candidate, validation and test entries
report/ The generated report, rebuilt on demand and never edited

Everything is plain text. A project can be read with any editor, kept on a shared drive or in git, and archived as it is.

An entry

Here is the trial, entry 0004, exactly as written:

cat(readLines(file.path(project, "entries", "0004-trial.yml")), sep = "\n")
#> # pdmS7 calibration log entry. Written once; never edit. verify_project() checks it.

#> id: '0004'

Every entry starts with the same header:

Field Content
format Entry format version
id Four-digit sequence number, as in the file name
type One of the eleven entry types
timestamp When it was written, UTC
author Declared name and role, and the operating-system login
software pdmS7 version, R version, platform and engine
previous Checksum (MD5) of the entry before it

The rest depends on the type. Numbers are written with the fewest digits that reproduce the exact value, so a configuration read back from the log is the configuration that ran.

The eleven entry types

Type Written by Role Key fields
project_start start_calibration_project() Custodian Catchment, gauge, purpose, area, Owner, Steward
data_registered register_data() Custodian Files and checksums, data quality, scoring windows, thresholds, headline
structure_selected select_structure() Custodian Configuration, scores, output checksum, reasoning
trial log_trial() Custodian Parent, changes, configuration, scores, output checksum, verdict, reasoning
auto_calibration log_auto_calibration(), compare_structures() Custodian Bounds, scales, method, objective, starts, every start’s result, configuration, scores
note log_note() Any Text and the entry it concerns
candidate propose_candidate() Custodian The run proposed, its scores, the saved series
validation validate_candidate() Custodian Validation scores beside calibration scores, saved series
test test_candidate() Custodian Test scores, scored once, saved series
sign_off sign_off_project() Steward or Delegated Steward Candidate, final configuration, checklist, statement
reopen reopen_project() Steward or Delegated Steward Reason

Trials, automatic calibrations and structures form a tree: every run names its parent, so the log records the path taken, dead ends included.

read_project(project)$entries[, .(id, type, author, summary)]
#>        id               type          author
#>    <char>             <char>          <char>
#> 1:   0001      project_start Ann Hydrologist
#> 2:   0002    data_registered Ann Hydrologist
#> 3:   0003 structure_selected Ann Hydrologist
#> 4:   0004              trial Ann Hydrologist
#> 5:   0005               note Ann Hydrologist
#> 6:   0006          candidate Ann Hydrologist
#> 7:   0007         validation Ann Hydrologist
#> 8:   0008               test Ann Hydrologist
#>                                   summary
#>                                    <char>
#> 1:           Example Brook - Illustration
#> 2:                               960 rows
#> 3:                          Standard PDM.
#> 4:                   fc 0.9 -> 1 (better)
#> 5: Gauge checked against the station log.
#> 6:                             Entry 0004
#> 7:                         Candidate 0006
#> 8:                  Candidate 0006 tested

The checksum chain

Each entry stores the checksum of the entry before it. Change one character of an earlier entry and its checksum changes, so the next entry’s previous no longer matches. Delete an entry, or slip one in, and the numbering or the chain breaks.

ids <- read_project(project)$entries$id
previous <- vapply(ids, function(i) read_entry(project, i)$previous, character(1))
k <- length(ids)
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
plot(NA, xlim = c(0.5, k + 0.5), ylim = c(0, 1), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
rect(seq_len(k) - 0.38, 0.35, seq_len(k) + 0.38, 0.75, col = "#eef4f6", border = pal[1])
text(seq_len(k), 0.62, ids, font = 2, cex = 0.85)
text(seq_len(k), 0.45, substr(previous, 1, 6), cex = 0.6, family = "mono", col = pal[5])
arrows(seq_len(k - 1) + 0.38, 0.55, seq_len(k - 1) + 0.62, 0.55, length = 0.06, col = pal[2])

Each entry’s ‘previous’ field holds the checksum of the entry before it (first six characters shown).

verify_project() walks the chain, checks every data and series file against its checksum and, with rerun = TRUE, repeats every run and compares the output checksum.

verify_project(project, rerun = TRUE)[, .N, by = .(check, ok)]
#>            check     ok     N
#>           <char> <lgcl> <int>
#> 1:     numbering   TRUE     8
#> 2:         chain   TRUE     8
#> 3:  data forcing   TRUE     1
#> 4: data observed   TRUE     1
#> 5:        series   TRUE     3
#> 6:         rerun   TRUE     4

Suppose someone tidies the reasoning of the trial after the event:

file <- file.path(project, "entries", "0004-trial.yml")
original <- readLines(file)
writeLines(sub("10 per cent", "8 per cent", original), file)
verify_project(project)[ok == FALSE]
#>     check  entry     ok                                      detail
#>    <char> <char> <lgcl>                                      <char>
#> 1:  chain   0005  FALSE Previous entry altered, removed or inserted
writeLines(original, file)

The edit to 0004 shows up at 0005, whose stored checksum no longer matches. Three details make the checks dependable in practice:

  • Line endings. Checksums ignore carriage returns, so a Windows checkout that converts line endings does not break the chain.
  • Output checksums are taken on flow rounded to 10 significant figures, so a project logged on one version of R verifies by rerun on another.
  • The newest entry has no successor to vouch for it. Sign-off, version control, or a managed drive covers it.

Writers take a lock on the project folder while appending, so two people working in one project on a shared drive cannot interleave entries.

The run log

The calibration log records how parameters were chosen; the run log records where they were used. It is off unless a path is set.

log_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "runs.csv")
register <- file.path(tempdir(), "approved.yml")
writeLines(c("projects:", paste0("  - ", basename(project))), register)

A register is a YAML file listing the projects whose signed-off configurations count as approved, with paths relative to the file:

cat(readLines(register), sep = "\n")
#> projects:
#>   - inside
options(pdmS7.run_log = log_file, pdmS7.register = register, pdmS7.run_tag = "example")
candidate <- read_entry(project, 6)$configuration
invisible(run_pdm(pdm_from_config(candidate), forcing[1:48, ]))
invisible(run_pdm(pdm_from_config(start), forcing[1:48, ]))
runs <- read_run_log(log_file)
names(runs)
#>  [1] "timestamp"   "user"        "login"       "tag"         "fingerprint"
#>  [6] "data_md5"    "rows"        "start"       "end"         "dt_hours"   
#> [11] "area_km2"    "engine"      "pdmS7"       "r"           "seconds"    
#> [16] "status"      "message"     "approval"    "project"     "sign_off"
runs[, .(tag, fingerprint = substr(fingerprint, 1, 8), rows, status, approval)]
#>        tag fingerprint  rows status   approval
#>     <char>      <char> <int> <char>     <char>
#> 1: example    c22081b9    48     ok unapproved
#> 2: example    24485fa7    48     ok unapproved
Column Content
timestamp, user, login, tag When, who, and an optional label from options(pdmS7.run_tag = )
fingerprint Checksum of the model’s components and parameters; see pdm_fingerprint()
data_md5, rows, start, end The forcing used
dt_hours, area_km2, engine, pdmS7, r Model and software
seconds, status, message Run time, and the error if it failed
approval, project, sign_off approved, superseded or unapproved, and the sign-off matched

Both runs show as unapproved: this project is validated and tested but not signed off. Once a Steward signs it off, runs with the candidate’s parameters are marked approved, with the project and sign-off entry; if the project is later reopened, they become superseded. Runs are never blocked.

The fingerprint recognises a model however it was built, from code, a preset or YAML, because it is taken on the model’s components and parameters, not on how they were written:

identical(pdm_fingerprint(candidate), pdm_fingerprint(pdm_from_config(candidate)))
#> [1] TRUE

Calibration evaluations, spin-up cycles and the calibration log’s own reruns are not logged, so the run log holds the runs people make. Logging is off by default, and a failure to write the log warns once and never stops a run.

Reading the logs

Function Returns
read_project() Project details, status and one row per entry
read_entry() One entry in full
project_trials() Every run with parent, changes, scores, verdict and reasoning
read_projects() One row per project, for a team folder or a large-sample batch
structure_comparison() A structure comparison’s ranking, rebuilt from the log
verify_project() The integrity checks
build_report() The report, as HTML and Markdown
read_run_log() The run log
approved_configurations() Every sign-off in a register, current or superseded
